subject.title: [Feature Request] SKILL.md Instruction Isolation from Agent Context

question: What security boundary should OpenClaw enforce between SKILL.md contents, higher-priority agent instructions, memory, and tool access?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent boundary affects prompt assembly, runtime tool policy, memory behavior, skill/plugin compatibility, and user trust semantics, so automation should not choose it unilaterally.

options.title: Approve a core isolation design first
options.body: Define trusted/untrusted precedence, per-skill capability metadata, runtime enforcement points, upgrade behavior, tests, and docs before implementation begins.

options.title: Start with manifest and scanner building blocks
options.body: Narrow this issue to a staged plan that lands inspectable capabilities and Markdown scanning first while leaving runtime enforcement to a later maintainer-approved design.

options.title: Defer to documentation and trusted skills only
options.body: Keep skills as trusted operator-installed instructions and document the trust model, accepting that this issue's requested runtime isolation will not be implemented now.

recommendation.title: Approve a core isolation design first
recommendation.body: Define trusted/untrusted precedence, per-skill capability metadata, runtime enforcement points, upgrade behavior, tests, and docs before implementation begins.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior issue review and relevant skills prompt history make steipete the clearest available owner for the security-boundary decision.
